## 3. The evidence that moved it

**Nature Medicine declares a benchmarking crisis in biomedical machine
learning** ([40200055](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40200055/)). This is the
single most consequential card in the first half of 2025, and it is the origin
of a claim the corpus later had to correct: April was recorded as the high-water
mark of negative clinical-AI evidence on the strength of "null randomized trials
plus a benchmarking-crisis editorial". The editorial is real. The null randomized
trials never existed — re-reading every month of 2025 under one rule found zero
titles stating a null for any AI intervention.

**And in the same month, the audit reaches the models themselves.**
[40251685](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40251685/) (*Genome Biol*): zero-shot
evaluation reveals limitations of single-cell foundation models. Read with the
benchmarking-crisis editorial, April 2025 is when the methods literature began
auditing the thing it had spent the previous year building — eight months before
this corpus recorded that as having happened.

**"Virtual cell" is already a *Nature Biotechnology* title**
([40229360](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40229360/), virtual cells for
predictive immunotherapy) — a comment proposing virtual-cell models for
predicting immunotherapy response, in print two months *before* the *Cell*
challenge usually credited with naming the concept. An earlier version of this
sentence added "and seven months before the phrase reaches the methods journals",
which encoded an arrival date `data/threads.yml` has since retracted; no interval
replaces it. Read the April title as a bound on the months that were read, not as
a date for the vocabulary. This corpus has made ten claims of that shape and has
retracted ten.

**An intracellular checkpoint reaches first-in-human.**
[40315882](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40315882/) (*Lancet Oncol*): CRISPR-Cas9
CISH-edited T cells in metastatic colorectal cancer. Note the shape — the target
is not blocked with an antibody, it is deleted in the cell being infused. That
manoeuvre becomes the class's main survival route by 2026.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[40249828](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40249828/) (*Sci Immunol*):
**CCR8-positive decidual regulatory T cells maintain maternal-fetal immune
tolerance in early pregnancy.** CCR8 is the marker chosen for effector-Treg
depletion precisely because it is supposed to be tumour-restricted. This is the
most direct card in the corpus against that premise, and the question it opens —
whether the chosen surface marker separates the subset that should go from the
one that should stay — is the one every depletion programme downstream of it has
to answer.

[40139188](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40139188/): metallophilic marginal zone
macrophages cross-prime protective CD8 immunity against blood-borne tumours,
matching cDC1s at cross-priming and depending on Batf3 rather than on handover
from cDC1s. A macrophage population whose depletion would remove antitumour
immunity rather than release it.

Against it, [40280128](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40280128/) is the
thread's clearest support: Treg depletion promotes myeloid activation and
glioblastoma response to anti-PD-1. Both directions are real, which is the point
of carding stance rather than topic.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    Three further cards were filed here as inversions and none of them is one.

    [40202509](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40202509/) was listed as
    "neutrophil MYO1F is *required* for the response to checkpoint blockade",
    read as a suppressive population being necessary for immunotherapy. The
    abstract runs the other way: tumour-associated neutrophils are a significant
    barrier, MYO1F is what restrains their suppression, and tumour-derived
    TGF-beta1 silencing it is what makes them suppressive. That is the canonical
    account, and the card now supports the thread.

    [40306958](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40306958/) was listed as
    tumour-infiltrating mast cells acting as a chemoimmunotherapy *enhancer*,
    which reads as a primary finding. It is a *JITC* commentary on Zhang et al.
    in *Cancer Cell*, a paper this corpus does not hold. The inversion it reports
    may well be real; this record is not evidence for it, and carding the echo
    rather than the study is how this corpus opened two threads on the wrong
    paper.

    [39786370](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39786370/) was filed as the
    adrenergic axis "cutting the other way in a clinical setting", against an
    intervention built on it. No such intervention was tested. Carvedilol and
    metoprolol are cardiac drugs, and the finding is that blocking beta2/beta3 —
    but not beta1 — signalling delays platelet engraftment and reduces survival
    after allogeneic transplant, in two patient cohorts and in mice. Neural
    control of a haematopoietic-immune process, demonstrated in humans, is the
    thread's mechanism claim rather than its contradiction. The setting is
    transplant engraftment, not a tumour microenvironment, and the card now
    supports.

### (b) Method credibility

[40205439](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40205439/): the standard
high-mitochondrial-content quality filter depletes viable, metabolically altered
malignant cells from cancer single-cell studies. A default QC step that
systematically removes the cells of interest.

[40197327](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40197327/): missing cell types in
single-cell references distort bulk deconvolution.
[40240607](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40240607/) (*Nature*): there is low
overlap between transcription factor DNA binding and regulatory targets — which
undercuts binding-derived regulatory networks generally.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    [40082610](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40082610/) was listed here as a
    third method-credibility refutation — "feature selection method choice
    changes integration and querying performance" — on the strength of a title
    that names its object rather than its verdict. The verdict runs the other
    way: benchmarking feature selection across integration, query mapping, label
    transfer and unseen-population detection, the paper states that it
    "reinforce[s] common practice by showing that highly variable feature
    selection is effective for producing high-quality integrations", and its
    output is guidance on how many features to take and when to take them
    batch-aware. This is the audit genre with the sign running the unexpected
    way: an audit that clears the method. It belongs on the supporting side.
